item.title: 2008: Phillies Win 4-3, Claim First Title Since 1980
item.description: Game 5 of the World Series is resumed at Citizens Bank Park in the bottom of the sixth inning after having been suspended October 27 because of rain. The Phillies win the game 4–3 to win their first title since 1980 and bring the city of Philadelphia a championship after 25 years. Pitcher Cole Hamels is named World Series MVP. Photo: Edg126 (CC BY-SA 3.0).

item.title: 2017: Astros Rally Past Dodgers 13-12 in 10 Innings, Lead Series
item.description: The Houston Astros came from behind three times to beat the visiting Los Angeles Dodgers, 13–12, in 10 innings in Game 5 of the World Series to take a 3–2 series lead. With their victory, the Astros became only the second team in history to overcome multiple three-run deficits in the same World Series game. Photo: The White House on Flickr (Public domain).

item.title: 2017: Al Richter, 90, Former Red Sox Shortstop
item.description: Al Richter, 90, shortstop who played for the Boston Red Sox in a span of two seasons from 1951 to 1953.

item.title: 2013: José Abreu Signs $68 Million Deal With White Sox
item.description: Cuban defector José Abreu agrees to a six-year, $68 million contract to play for the Chicago White Sox. It is the largest deal ever handed out by an international free agent in Major League history, besting the six-year, $60 million contract the Texas Rangers gave Yu Darvish on January 20, 2012. Photo: EricEnfermero (CC BY-SA 4.0).

item.title: 2013: Aeros Become Akron RubberDucks, Honoring Rubber Capital
item.description: On October 29, 2013, the Aeros changed their name to the Akron RubberDucks, paying homage to Akron as the original "Rubber Capital of the World" and celebrating the family entertainment aspect of Minor League Baseball.

item.title: 2011: Angels Hire Jerry Dipoto as 11th General Manager
item.description: The Los Angeles Angels hire Jerry Dipoto as their new general manager. Dipoto becomes the 11th GM in club history.

item.title: 2010: Wilson Named 13th Manager of Kane County Cougars
item.description: On October 29, 2010, Wilson was named the 13th manager of the Kane County Cougars, the Kansas City Royals' Class A Midwest League affiliate.

item.title: 2010: Mets Name Sandy Alderson Their New General Manager
item.description: The New York Mets name Sandy Alderson their new general manager. Photo: Chamber of Fear; cropped by Beyond My Ken (talk) 02:52, 8 July 2011 (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2009: Yankees Even World Series With 3-1 Win Over Phillies
item.description: The New York Yankees even the World Series at a game apiece with a 3–1 victory against the Philadelphia Phillies. In the biggest start of his career, A. J. Burnett throws seven solid innings to get his first postseason win, holding the Phillies to only one run and four hits, while Mark Teixeira and Hideki Matsui provide the offensive support with solo home runs off Pedro Martínez, the losing pitcher. Photo: Samantha Appleton (Public domain).

item.title: 2007: Speier Signed by Reds as Infield Coach
item.description: Speier was signed by the Cincinnati Reds on October 29, 2007, as an infield coach and served as the Reds' bench coach. Photo: Dealphungo (CC BY-SA 3.0).

item.title: 2006: Silas Simmons, 109, Longest-Lived Pro Baseball Player
item.description: Silas Simmons, 109 (or 111), Negro leagues player of the 1920s, believed to be the longest-lived professional baseball player in history.

item.title: 1995: Al Niemiec, 84, Former Red Sox Second Baseman
item.description: Al Niemiec, 84, second baseman who played with the Boston Red Sox in the 1934 season and for the Philadelphia Athletics in 1936. Photo: Apex Photograph Company (Public domain).

item.title: 1994: Yomiuri Giants Win Game 6, Claim Japan Series Title
item.description: The Yomiuri Giants win Game 6 of the Japan Series to become professional baseball's World Champions. Legend says this is the luckiest of all championship years, as it is the team's sixtieth anniversary, as they are deemed world champions by some baseball media.

item.title: 1991: Yankees Promote Buck Showalter to Replace Stump Merrill
item.description: The New York Yankees announce that Buck Showalter has been promoted to replace Stump Merrill as manager. Photo: Keith Allison from Hanover, MD, USA (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 1988: Andy Cohen, 84, Former Giants Second Baseman
item.description: Andy Cohen, 84, second baseman who hit .281 in 262 games with the New York Giants from 1926 to 1929; acting manager of 1960 Philadelphia Phillies for one game (April 14) between terms of Eddie Sawyer and Gene Mauch; younger brother Syd, an MLB pitcher, died earlier in 1988 (on April 9).

item.title: 1986: White Sox Name Larry Himes, 46, General Manager
item.description: The Chicago White Sox make a course correction in their front office, naming Larry Himes, 46, vice president and general manager, and accepting the resignation of GM Tom Haller, a left-over from the failed Ken Harrelson experiment.

item.title: 1981: Phillies Sold to Investment Group for $30.175 Million
item.description: Third-generation owner Ruly Carpenter sells the Philadelphia Phillies to a five-member investment group that includes club executive Bill Giles, son of the late president of the National League, for $30.175 million—the highest price then paid for a baseball franchise. Carpenter's grandfather and father had purchased the Phillies for $500,000 in 1943.

item.title: 1969: Jim Bunning Returns to Phillies as Free Agent
item.description: Right-hander Jim Bunning returns to the Philadelphia Phillies as a free agent after being released one week earlier by the Los Angeles Dodgers. Bunning, 38, had gone 74–46 for the Phils between 1964 and 1967. Photo: From collection of JGHowes, self-scanned for Wikipedia. JGHowes at (Public domain).

item.title: 1963: Yankees Release Yogi Berra to Make Him Manager
item.description: The New York Yankees release catcher and playing coach Yogi Berra, 38, so he can manage the 1964 Bombers. He succeeds Ralph Houk, who moves up to general manager, replacing the retiring Roy Hamey. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1962: Yankees Sell Bob Turley Contract to Angels
item.description: The New York Yankees sell the contract of one-time ace right-hander Bob Turley to the Los Angeles Angels. Turley, 32, has been struggling with arm woes since his banner 1958 season, when he won the Cy Young Award and was named MVP of the 1958 World Series. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1944: Carolina League Announced After Durham Meeting
item.description: The Carolina League was announced on October 29, 1944, after an organizational meeting at Durham, North Carolina.

item.title: 1889: Giants Win Second Straight World Series, Beat Bridegrooms 3-2
item.description: The New York Giants win their second consecutive World Series title by beating the Brooklyn Bridegrooms, 3–2, for their fifth straight win in taking the series 6 games to 3. Photo: J Wood, 208 Bowery, N.Y. (Public domain).
